previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for acute nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. He was dehydrated with tachycardia on presentation. Workup for bacterial infection, including C. diff, stool culture, and ova and parasites, was negative, and symptoms were attributed to viral gastroenteritis, likely contracted from a sick family member. IV fluids were given, and empiric Zosyn was started but discontinued due to lack of bacterial source. A brief course of cefepime was given for concern over skin secretion changes but stopped after no signs of active infection. Liver enzymes were elevated but stable, thought to be secondary to viral illness. The patient improved clinically, resumed oral intake, and was discharged home. He received the first dose of abatacept as part of a clinical trial for refractory chronic GVHD and tolerated it well. Discharge medications included oral ciprofloxacin, amoxicillin (now dosed every 12 hours), and all baseline immunosuppressive and prophylactic regimens.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

You were admitted to the hospital due to worsening pain in your 
lower legs and feet and concern for infection. You were seen by 
our infectious disease and wound care specialists, who felt that 
your feet were not infected and looked a little better since the 
last time they saw them. Because of the pain, you were seen by 
our pain medicine specialists, and had gabapentin and tramadol 
added to your medication regimen. This seemed to control your 
pain better, and you were discharged home to follow up with Dr. 
___ as an outpatient. 

We wish you the best,
Your ___ Care Team 

New wound care recommendations:
Wound Care:

1. Soak all dressings with normal saline or commercial wound
cleanser daily, and remove gently.

2. Wash the wounds with 0.25% Acetic acid daily. Rinse with
normal saline.

4. Apply thin layer Santyl ointment (chemical debridement agent)
to all wounds beds with yellow/green slough.

5. Place Adaptic dressing over all wounds, and below toes dorsal
foot.

6. Place Softsorb dressing mid arch area to each foot.

7. Apply Kerlix wrap from below toes to below knee.

8. Secure with tape.

9. Change dressings daily.

10. Schedule follow up visit with CWOCN in 2 weeks @ BMT
outpatient clinic.
